messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: service=redwood-inference api=streaming generation latency p99 > 3.0s (SLO breach) -- triggered by kv-cache pressure spike, region eu-west-1. Incident severity: P1 :rotating_light:
maya (on-call): I'm on it. paging joel and sasha. starting triage. maya -> joining grafana now
joel (sre): I'm looking at the p95/p99 dashboards. seeing p95 ~ 450ms, p99 ~ 3.6s for streaming endpoints. spikes correlate with high prefill activity on a subset of shards.
sasha (runtime): initial hypothesis: prefill vs decode imbalance — too many prefill requests filling KV slab, eviction churn causing tail stalls during decode. logs show increased `kv.prefill_bytes` and concurrent `kv.decode` latency skew.
oliver (support): multiple customers reported degraded chat streaming (tokens arriving in big chunks). raised two high-priority tickets — customers A and B seeing timeouts on 3rd-party SDKs. marking customer-impacting.
priya (prod-eng): what's the % of streaming traffic affected? need to flag billing/CS.
joel (sre): approx 12% of streaming requests from eu-west-1 have p99 > 3s in last 10m, error rate unchanged. So functionality ok, but tail latency + stalls.
maya (on-call): can we get a quick mitigations list. prioritise actions that avoid restart first.
sasha (runtime): mitigation options I can do now: 1) throttle prefill traffic by route 2) change prefill balancer to prefer non-congested slabs 3) temporarily disable aggressive prefill on long-context sessions 4) increase eviction threshold (risk memory spike)
dan (infra): I can push a traffic-split to route 30% of streaming to a warm fallback cluster in us-west-2 to reduce eu-west load. latency to some customers might increase but lowers tail stalls. want go/no-go?
oliver (support): customers asked for ETA. any quick fix we can tell them? Jaime on CS asks for a 30-min estimate.
joel (sre): immediate plan: (A) throttle prefill at the gateway for eu-west-1 (rate limit new prefill requests) -> low risk, quick. (B) route 20% streaming to fallback cluster (dan can do). (C) Sasha to patch prefill balancer weights to avoid hot slabs. If those don't reduce p99 in 10m, escalate to slab resize + rolling restarts.
priya (prod-eng): 👍 agree. also add a metric alert for prefill/ decode ratio and eviction rate for postmortem.
sasha (runtime): executing patch: reducing prefill concurrency from 6->2 for streaming sessions in eu-west-1. applying config now: ```curl -XPOST https://config-api/patch -d '{"service":"prefill","region":"eu-west-1","concurrency":2}'```
deploy-bot: deploy started by sasha for config prefill-reduce-eu-west-1 (cid 7b9f)
maya (on-call): dan, can you start the routing play?
dan (infra): starting traffic-split now. running `balancerctl split --from eu-west-1 --to us-west-2 --percent 20 --route streaming`
deploy-bot: traffic-split applied (change id ts-761234)
joel (sre): watching metrics: p99 dropped from 3.6s -> 2.1s in first 4m; p95 unchanged. eviction rate down 35%. good signal.
oliver (support): passing interim update to customers: "We're actively mitigating a latency issue affecting streaming in eu-west-1; we've throttled prefill activity and routed some traffic to fallback capacity — service is degraded but recovering. We'll update in 15m."
sasha (runtime): patched prefill balancer weights to avoid shards 12/13/14 which were hot. configured new weight map. applied. logs show prefill ops redistributed.
joel (sre): after 12m p99 ~1.8s, streaming stalls instances significantly reduced. but tail still high on a small subset of requests. digging deeper into decode queue backlog.
maya (on-call): are there any pods with sustained high `aio_read` or `kv.decode` latencies?
luis (infra): yes a handful of decode workers on shard 14 show queue depth spike and CPU load ~92%. memory within limits. I can spin up 2 extra decode workers on those hosts.
dan (infra): provisioning 2 workers now. `provisioner start-workers --count 2 --role decode --shard 14 --region eu-west-1`
deploy-bot: provision job queued -> success (job id prov-9834)
joel (sre): after extra workers came up, backlog cleared on shard 14, p99 for that subset dropped to ~1.3s. overall p99 now ~1.6s. we are still above target SLO (1.0s) but trending down.
priya (prod-eng): good progress. recommend customer-facing post in 30m with details and follow-up ticket.
maya (on-call): preparing handoff notes. won't escalate to slab resize for now. We'll keep throttles and routing for 1 hour, monitor. If p99 < 1.2s stable for 20m, start rollback of routing.
joel (sre): root-cause hypothesis to record: prefill surge concentrated on small shard subset causing slab churn and eviction noise; prefill vs decode imbalance (prefill concurrency > decode throughput) produced tail stalls during streaming.
sasha (runtime): follow-ups: 1) add adaptive prefill backpressure when eviction rate > X 2) make balancer shard-weight changes automatic under load 3) add per-shard decode autoscaler 4) run load replay to validate fix.
dan (infra): ops action: temporary runbook updates pushed to oncall-runbooks — `mitigate-kv-prefill-surge` with steps we executed.
olm (typo-bot): (ignore)
maya (on-call): handing to joel for next shift at 23:00 UTC. joel, please pick up monitoring for next 2 hours and coordinate with runtime infra.
joel (sre): taking it. summary: throttles applied, 20% traffic routed to fallback, prefill weights adjusted, extra decode workers added. watch p99 + eviction_rate + prefill/decode ratio. will update every 15m.
priya (prod-eng): assigning postmortem owners: sasha + joel. expected doc in 72h. include customer impact timeline and mitigations.
oliver (support): raising postmortem ticket for affected customers and drafting CS note.
maya (on-call): closing incident channel for now. if anything regresses -> reopen. great work team :clap:
